issues.message: The assertion that the normalized shifted argument lies in a fixed compact subregion of the inverse disk is false on the claimed complex dented neighborhood. Write t=S-y and S'=t+u for the principal m=1 shifted center; its normalized argument is u/(t+u). For real S>0, choose phi in (3pi/4,pi-gamma_H), t=epsilon exp(i phi), y=S-t and u=tau y with tau=-epsilon cos(phi)/S. As epsilon tends to zero, |u/(t+u)| tends to |cot(phi)|>1, although u is in the initial O(|t|) segment and y is in the stated dented region. Consequently the stated disk-based justification of the uniform initial integral is unavailable. Approved B contains the stronger cone estimates needed for a local repair, but their actual hypotheses and derivative scale must be applied here.
issues.requested_change: Replace the inverse-disk assertion by a proof that (S',u) remains in a strictly smaller small-|S'| critical two-distance cone, using the kernel-shift preservation in Lemma B.4 and the near-critical extension/patching in Proposition B.12. On |u|<=C|t|, verify |S'| is comparable to |t|, S'-u=t and S'+u=t+2u are separated from zero at that scale, with fixed angular margins. Then apply (B.28) on the larger cone to obtain |partial_s L_h(theta;s,u)|<=C|t|^((h-1)/2-1) (or the corresponding fixed mixed-derivative bound), and multiply by the O(|t|) path length. Keep the common complex domain and additive error claimed by Proposition 8.8; a real-axis-only argument does not suffice for coefficient transfer. Use an endpoint-distance name distinct from the inherited descendant t_0 while revising this local passage.
